jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Stand is a homeowners insurance carrier for people who live where wildfire and hurricanes are a fact of life. The promise we make them is unusual: we try to reach you before the loss and get you help, and we handle the claim fast when it comes. This role owns both ends of that promise. Right now there is no single person who owns catastrophe readiness and response across Stand. Someone has to build the plan before a season, hold our claims partners to a real standard every day, and then run the whole thing when an event is bearing down on our customers. Without that, the promise is a slogan; with it, it's something a homeowner can count on. Concretely, the job is three things. You build and keep current the catastrophe plan, covering activation levels, who does what, vendor capacity, regulatory reporting, and how we reach customers and brokers. You manage the third-party administrators who handle our claims, day to day and against their service standards. And you own the Emergency Response Program: the work that finds policyholders in the path of an event and gets them help, increasingly automated, with people kept in the loop for the judgment calls. You report to the Head of Claims and Client Experience and work across the company. jobs.title: Device - Software Engineer (Functional Safety)
jobs.description_text: OUR MISSION SPAN develops products that accelerate the rapid adoption of renewable energy in the home. The flagship SPAN Smart Panel is the first true evolution for the traditional home electric panel, harnessing enhanced technology for metering, monitoring, and control. An expanded product suite of intelligent, integrated solutions radically lowers the cost and complexity of energy upgrades–including solar, batteries and EVs–empowering homeowners to be active, resilient and informed players in the energy market. THE TEAM AND ROLE SPAN's Device Software team is responsible for all of the software that is physically embodied in our hardware products. The Gen3 SPAN Panel is a distributed system of STM32H5 (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontroller modules that talk over CAN, meter power in real time, and open or close relays that sit directly between the grid, the home and its solar, battery and EV equipment. When that firmware makes a decision, real current moves. We are building a dedicated Functional Safety (FuSa) firmware capability to take Gen3 firmware through certification as a Power Control System under UL 3141 and as Class B control software under UL/IEC 60730-1 Annex H. This is not a checkbox exercise: FuSa at SPAN spans how we architect and partition the firmware, how we detect faults and drive the system into defined safe states, how we test and prove coverage, and how we document and trace every safety requirement back to code. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Real-Time Generalist
jobs.description_text: The Opportunity Most full stack roles ask you to move pixels around a dashboard. This one asks you to help architect the system that controls the largest drone swarm on the planet. You’ll join the team building Legion, Swarm Aero’s Command & Control platform. Legion enables a single operator to plan, direct, and execute missions across a networked swarm of heterogeneous aircraft in real time, over intermittent communications, and at a scale nobody else in the industry is attempting. This is not a role maintaining a finished product or adding features around the edges. You’ll help define the architecture, establish core technical patterns, and build entirely new capabilities for a problem space with little prior art. The work spans real-time distributed systems, dense telemetry visualization, collaborative mission planning, and operator interfaces where clarity and reliability directly affect mission outcomes. You’ll have meaningful influence over what we build, how we build it, and how the platform evolves as the team and system scale. What You'll Do - Partner directly with developers to secure the product across the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), embedding security early rather than bolting it on at the end. - Lead security design and architecture reviews, and run threat modeling on new features and services. - Perform hands-on penetration testing of web applications and Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), and translate findings into clear, prioritized, fixable work. - Conduct secure code reviews and help define secure-coding standards and security acceptance criteria. - Operate and tune Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and dependency / supply-chain scanning, and triage what they surface. - Help engineers understand the "why" behind findings so the same class of issue doesn't recur. - Contribute security evidence and rigor to our compliance posture (System and Organization Controls 2, or SOC 2, ISO 270
